title: Check yourself: Builders, students and educators

questions.stem: A developer asks Claude for a data-import function, pastes it into the codebase and ships it after a glance because it reads cleanly. Which habit did the developer skip?

options.text: Responsibility: tell the users that an AI assisted with the release
options.says: Ruled out because telling users is honest but does not test anything, and the natural check is to "Run it, test it, review it".

options.text: Delegation: hand the whole function to a different person to write instead
options.says: Ruled out because "A builder is someone who owns the whole arc from a customer's problem to a shipped solution", so the function is theirs to verify.

options.text: Description: phrase the request as a longer, more detailed paragraph
options.says: Ruled out because the weight for builders falls on "Discernment of code and user experience", and a longer request does not test the result.

options.text: Discernment: execute it against realistic cases and inspect the results
options.says: The builder's costly mistake is "Shipping unrun output", and the natural check is to "Run it, test it, review it".

questions.stem: A university student drafts a graded argumentative essay. The course allows AI help for planning only, and they want to find where their case is weakest. Which use fits?

options.text: Ask Claude for a model paragraph on their topic, then rewrite it in their voice
options.says: Ruled out because "writing the analysis with Claude and submitting it defeats the point and may breach the institution's rules", and rewording a model paragraph still hands the thinking over.

options.text: Have Claude draft their weakest section, cite it as a source, and write the rest themselves
options.says: Ruled out because the student does not delegate "the thinking the course exists to build", and a citation does not return it.

options.text: Paste the essay prompt and keep only the sentences that match their view
options.says: Ruled out because "one who submits its essay as their own is not" using it as a partner, and selecting sentences keeps that authorship problem.

options.text: Ask Claude to challenge their outline, then do all the writing themselves
options.says: A student uses Claude as a partner by questioning the plan while the thinking and the writing stay theirs.

questions.stem: A teacher asks Claude for a quiz on a unit and gets ten questions. Which step best reflects discernment and ownership?

options.text: Share it with the class so the pupils can find any faults
options.says: Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how they are assessed and the fairness of grades", and passing the checking to pupils gives that up.

options.text: Trust it, because the model wrote a similar quiz last month
options.says: Ruled out because the educator "Checks: accuracy of the content taught", and a past good quiz does not show this one is right.

options.text: Check the answers and their fit with the stated outcome
options.says: Discernment is judging accuracy and alignment with the stated outcome, and the educator owns what students are taught.

options.text: Ask Claude to rate how correct its own questions are
options.says: Ruled out because asking Claude to mark itself is not the check, and the page lists "accuracy of the content taught" among the things the educator checks personally.
